content.text: Is the task here to provide a bunch of different spring configurations in different folders that someone can copy over the default and build to get their desired setup or is it to just document the sections of the various configuration files that need to be edited to enable the various features?

I was thinking about consolidating the various spring configuration files into a single one, with commented out sections for various modules. This would also be accompanied by some documentation, potentially in the fcrepo-webapp-plus readme.md, that describes who the meaning of the configuration elements and how/why to enable them.
I would like to:
1. get away from having to generate build artifacts for the permutations of optional modules, and
2. highlight to the community a more flexible approach to site-specific wiring of components.
I will also note that the actual implementation of this ticket may take on a different flavor once the details surface in the course of the work.
Just as an FYI, here is a project that builds the Fedora webapp using a single spring XML file. Feel free to use this as inspiration:
https://gitlab.amherst.edu/acdc/amherst-fedora-webapp
nice
Very cool
, I will have a look at that and see if I can make this happen.
Would I also be providing a default
repository.json
in the fcrepo-webapp-plus to allow for the configuration you need there (specifically around authentication)?
I was thinking that this task is to update fcrepo-webapp-plus such that there is only one maven profile that is not active by default. This profile turns web.xml configuration of AuthZ on.
Would it make sense to have two repository.json files for the AuthZ and non-AuthZ scenarios?
Also, should I move the optional dependencies up in pom.xml...and comment them out or leave them in like the new AppleTree one?
Probably make them included all of the time... unless there are specific AuthZ dependencies that can stay in the profile.
Ok, so...we can do that. Would the AuthZ enabled web.xml refer to the same
configuration.xml
as the non-AuthZ enabled web.xml? But before you build it you need to open and change the configuration in it?
Here is what I have for the config files so you can see what I'm doing.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/compare/master...whikloj:FCREPO-2389?expand=1
What you have in the code diff looks good.
The web.xml actually points to a
repository.xml
that is configured to potentially use a user-provided
configuration.xml
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/compare/master...whikloj:FCREPO-2389?expand=1#diff-62faf366056ce148613dc8d031b9c86aR8
I trust your judgement over if it makes more sense to have another example
configuration.xml
for AuthZ, or if commented sections are sufficient.
In any case, the high-level recommendation for users will be to use their own, externalized
configuration.xml
PR -
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/55
Thanks for your patience,
, as we iterator on this a couple of times... but what you have here looks great.
Tried to make the changes requested. Let me know if anything is unclear.
I edited the logback, and was thinking about not providing one and just let the one from fcrepo-webapp get carried through. However that one also has entries for transform and connector still in it.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/55
This looks good, with some minor code review comments.
Once we close this ticket, the natural follow-on is to provide a similar consolidated configuration pattern for the core webapp:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2393
New commit on
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/55
One last minor code review comment... then this should be good to go.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/commit/17c7836368fbcb350c177db4be6fdd1bb81aa3eb
PR for 4.7-maintenance:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/59
Resolved on 4.7-maintanence with
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/commit/bbe8abae786f1e3e850818a684a4e4e68e19e8cd
This task is to update fcrepo-webapp-plus such that there is only one maven profile that is not active by default.
This profile turns web.xml configuration of AuthZ on.
The other components (audit, webac, rbacl, xacml, mint) should have example spring.xml configuration(s) along with documentation for describing:
how to enable these components and
how to reference such a configuration via system properties.
